title: Sahara: a network that moved
hook: Were caravan routes fixed for centuries?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.

objective: Caravan networks changed with goldfields, climate and political connections.

claims.text: Late 600s: Wider links. Caravans expand trans-Saharan exchange networks.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/exhibitions/sahel-art-empire-sahara/inside-the-exhibition — Early networks; Soninke Diasporas; Trade and Islam

claims.text: 1100s: Goldfields. Buré goldfields draw routes east and south.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/exhibitions/sahel-art-empire-sahara/inside-the-exhibition — Early networks; Soninke Diasporas; Trade and Islam

claims.text: 1200s: Drought. Drought contributes to Soninke dispersal.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/exhibitions/sahel-art-empire-sahara/inside-the-exhibition — Early networks; Soninke Diasporas; Trade and Islam

claims.text: 1324: Connections. Mansa Musa travels via Cairo toward Mecca.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/exhibitions/sahel-art-empire-sahara/inside-the-exhibition — Early networks; Soninke Diasporas; Trade and Islam

claims.text: Caravan networks changed with goldfields, climate and political connections. The opening of Buré’s goldfields shifted routes; drought contributed to dispersal; the 1324 pilgrimage linked Mali with Cairo and beyond. These networks also carried enslaved people, alongside goods and ideas.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/exhibitions/sahel-art-empire-sahara/inside-the-exhibition — Early networks; Soninke Diasporas; Trade and Islam

claims.text: Lines summarize changing connections, not exact caravan tracks or complete trade volumes.
